frontmatter.title: Two Ways from Tidy to Wide
frontmatter.subtitle: DS 2023 | Communicating with Data

children.value: This notebook introduces a recipe for create a wide table from a tidy table.

children.value: It describes two method for doing so under two conditions.
: Do the two grouping variables combine to produce a unique set over the observations or not?

flowchart TD C["Check if g1 x g2 combinations are unique over D by using D.value_counts(['g1','g2'])"] C --> D{"Does every count == 1?"} D -->|"Yes: each pair occurs
at most once"| E["Pure reshape
no aggregation needed"] D -->|"No: some pairs repeat"| F["Need to reshape and collapse with aggregation, e.g. mean"] E --> E1["D.pivot(index='g1',
columns='g2',
values='m')"] E --> E2["D.set_index(['g1','g2'])['m']
.unstack('g2')"] F --> F1["D.pivot_table(index='g1',
columns='g2',
values='m',
aggfunc='mean')"] F --> F2["D.groupby(['g1','g2'])['m']
.mean()['g2'].unstack()"] E1 --> Z["W: rows = G1 levels, cols = G2 levels, cells = M"] E2 --> Z F1 --> Z F2 --> Z classDef unique fill:#d8f0d8,stroke:#4a8a4a,color:#1c3a1c classDef dup fill:#fde4d4,stroke:#c07a45,color:#4a2a12 classDef err fill:#f8d7da,stroke:#a94442,color:#5a1d20 class E,E1,E2 unique class F,F1,F2 dup class W err
